picks.headline: New dev tool from Meta enables AI to quickly test Quest games
picks.excerpt: Meta introduced Meta XR Operator, an experimental tool that lets AI coding agents autonomously build, test, debug and visually verify VR apps on Quest.
picks.rationale: A shipping, hands-on tool: coding agents can now build, run and visually verify Quest builds, which changes an XR team's iteration loop tomorrow.

picks.headline: "We view AI as a sliding scale. There will always be a human in the loop": Why Side signed an MOU with Modl.ai to use AI for QA
picks.excerpt: Side and Modl.ai discuss the role of AI in games quality assurance, the tech's current limitations, and why human QA experts remain an essential part of the pipeline.
picks.rationale: The largest external QA vendor formalising AI in its pipeline — a concrete map of which QA work moves to agents and which stays human.

picks.headline: Tencent Games Central Tech debuts at Gamescom 2026 with AI tools spanning animation, gameplay, and testing
picks.excerpt: Tencent unveiled Motus, an AI pipeline for 3D animation, alongside GIGA and WeTest — a full-stack toolchain covering asset creation, gameplay and automated testing.
picks.rationale: A first public look at Tencent's in-house AI toolchain — Motus for 3D animation plus asset and automated-test tools — i.e. what an AI-native production stack looks like end to end.

picks.headline: 24% of Gamescom reveals officially used AI
picks.excerpt: 23.64% of the games featured during Gamescom Opening Night Live this year disclosed AI use in development or marketing — 13 of 55 titles shown.
picks.rationale: A hard number on disclosed AI use across a flagship showcase — the clearest available benchmark for how normalised AI in production has become.

picks.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 will have no microtransactions or generative AI
picks.excerpt: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson reportedly confirmed that no generative AI was used in GTA 6's development, and that the game ships without microtransactions.
picks.rationale: The industry's biggest release explicitly opting out of generative AI — the strongest counter-signal to the disclosure trend in the same week.
